requirement_text: This document is self-contained. A compliant implementation or reviewer must not need an earlier architecture document to determine intended subsystem behaviour.
Earlier architecture documents are historical only after ratification. When they conflict with this document, this document controls.
Current codebase compliance is recorded in separate dated reports that cite requirement IDs. Implementation status is never embedded in this permanent architecture.
Requirement IDs are never reused for a different meaning. Removed requirements remain reserved and are marked deprecated in later revisions.
An implementation limitation remains a limitation. It must not become a new architectural rule unless this document is explicitly revised.
A type, field, counter, diagnostic, test fixture, or interface declaration does not by itself satisfy a capability. Required mechanisms must participate causally through production paths.

Current languages, engines, libraries, processor placement, GPU layouts, brain-size classes, constants, adapters, and test fixtures are implementation mechanisms unless this document explicitly locks their semantics.
Develop artificial animals capable of increasingly general lifelong learning, grounded prediction, memory, concept formation, social learning, planning, communication, and transfer.
Maximize behavioural capability per unit of neural compute, memory, latency, biochemical work, teacher/SLM cost, and simulated energy.
Preserve evolvability: the organism must remain capable of useful genetic, developmental, biochemical, neural, and cultural adaptation rather than becoming one frozen engineered policy.
Remain a fun, legible persistent simulation game built around individual creatures, relationships, communities, teaching, breeding, culture, ecology, and visible behavioural change.
Use biologically inspired mechanisms when they improve intelligence, efficiency, robustness, evolvability, individuality, or game value; biological resemblance is never an end in itself.
Support extraction, enlargement, transplantation, and reuse of mature cognitive cores in other games, software environments, and embodied robots.
Keep the architecture inspectable and falsifiable so that apparent intelligence can be attributed to the creature rather than hidden host code, teachers, SLMs, or benchmark leakage.
All creature cognition is grounded in causal world, body, biochemical, memory, social, and teacher interactions. No privileged semantic truth may silently enter the brain.
The world reports physical and transactional facts, not reward, desirability, task success, or what the creature ought to do.
Every mutable fact has one authoritative owner. Other representations are explicitly derived views and cannot advance independently.
Genetics/development, body/physiology, biochemistry, and brain/cognitive memory are separate mechanisms with explicit interfaces and no duplicated ownership.
Computation and storage are bounded by explicit phenotype, world, or platform budgets. Unbounded all-pairs search, unbounded graph growth, and unbounded external-model calls are prohibited.
No hidden host policy may choose creature actions, fabricate learning credit, inject concepts or memories, or solve semantic tasks outside the creature.
Personal episodic memories, individual semantic propositions, current activations, current chemistry, pending eligibility, and autobiographical identity are not inherited biologically.
Teacher and semantic-prior services may accelerate learning but may not substitute for the creature brain. Competence must be separately measurable with each service removed.

The ordinary game, training/evaluation hosts, school system, and research scenarios must use the same semantic causal organism step. Reduced evaluators may exist only when explicitly labelled and may not certify full-organism capabilities.
Failure must be explicit. Missing assets, incompatible schemas, invalid causal transactions, and partial multi-system commits may not silently fall back to plausible defaults.
Brain, body, biochemistry, world, memory, persistence, lifecycle, and presentation must describe the same individual organism and causal sequence.

Architectural success is behavioural and causal, not ornamental. A biological mechanism that adds cost without measurable capability, robustness, game value, or evolvability must be replaceable or removable.
The canonical organism record binds organism identity to its genome/development state, body, biochemistry, brain ownership, memories, lifecycle, persistence dependencies, and presentation identity.
A subsystem may cache another subsystem's state only as a versioned read-only view tied to a causal tick or transaction ID.
No evaluator, UI, teacher, trainer, or adapter may maintain an independently advancing copy of canonical body, biochemical, developmental, neural, or memory state.
Every action/outcome cycle has a stable organism ID, causal sequence ID, pre-action state reference, decision reference, measured joint outcome, and commit status.
A transaction touching several authoritative systems either commits all required state transitions or rolls back all of them.
Causal sequence order is explicit and deterministic for identical initial state, inputs, configuration, and randomness seeds.
Neural, biochemical, metabolic, ecological, developmental, reproductive, and presentation cadences are not forced to one universal tick rate.
Each derived view records the authoritative tick or interval from which it was derived. Stale views are rejected when semantic freshness matters.
Catch-up processing is bounded. Large time jumps use capped substeps, analytically equivalent integration, or explicit approximation receipts rather than unbounded loops.
The simulation supports accelerated time while preserving births, deaths, learning, chemical dynamics, sleep, culture, and ecology within declared fidelity limits.

High-bandwidth neural updates normally run on the GPU; sparse irregular memory, concept, structural proposal, persistence, teacher, and world operations normally run on the CPU or service best suited to them. Placement is determined by measured efficiency, not authority ideology.

World sensing exposes grounded observables: geometry, motion, material/chemical cues, sound, light, contact, temperature, object persistence, social signals, and other physically or socially instantiated properties.

The world may expose that an effector can contact, grip, ingest, emit sound, or apply force. It may not expose that an entity is food, an enemy, a tool, desirable, dangerous, or the correct task target unless that information is itself communicated through a grounded world channel.
World action execution returns a measured joint physical outcome for the complete factorized motor bundle, including contacts, transfers, movement, damage, energy/material exchange, and failures.
Ecologies support resource scarcity, niches, hazards, social interaction, construction or manipulation, reproduction, and persistent environmental consequences sufficient for selection and culture.
Natural selection operates through survival, reproduction, resource access, and ecological consequence. The runtime brain is not trained by a hidden world fitness scalar.
Environmental complexity is introduced progressively so that founders can survive, but later worlds vary enough to prevent one fixed engineered policy from dominating all niches.
Body and physiology own physical morphology, tissue and organ state, energy reserves, injury, temperature, proprioception, actuator limits, and viability.
The body never stores reward, learned value, concepts, intentions, or semantic action preferences.
Organisms may differ genetically and developmentally in size, morphology, sensors, effectors, metabolism, resilience, lifespan, fertility, and physiological trade-offs.
Local organ or tissue dysfunction may alter behaviour and survival without immediately collapsing every other subsystem.
Body events report physical facts such as tissue damage, nutrient intake, material transfer, temperature change, force, displacement, social contact, and actuator effort.
A body event never contains a field whose semantics are equivalent to reward, punishment, task success, or preferred action.
Simple withdrawal, balance, actuator protection, and life-preserving reflexes may bypass deliberative cognition, but their stimuli and outcomes remain available to the brain for learning.
A reflex may prevent catastrophic harm; it may not silently solve a semantic or strategic task that the creature is expected to learn.
Physiology is represented as typed organs and tissues with local cadence, energetic cost, damage, repair, and exposed loci, rather than one undifferentiated health scalar.
Initial founder bodies use a manageable early-animal or early-mammal reference morphology; the architecture does not lock one species body plan.
The genome contains only heritable construction, development, mutation, recombination, and prior-reference information. It does not contain current acquired state.
The genome can alter body, organ, biochemical, neural, developmental, reproductive, temperament, plasticity, and learning characteristics.
The genome expresses separate body, biochemical, neural, and embodiment phenotypes. Shared traits may influence several phenotypes only through explicit compiler rules.

Biochemical parameters are not duplicated as independently authoritative brain constants. Neural receptor genes may refer to biochemical species or receptor classes without transferring ownership of chemistry into the brain genome.
Ordinary reproduction supports diploid or otherwise explicitly modelled recombination, mutation, dominance/codominance where used, lineage provenance, and compatibility checks.
Structural genetic variation may alter region allocation, create or suppress derived-region alleles, change biochemical graph topology, and change developmental timing within viability bounds.
A child receives new organism, brain, neuron, synapse, memory, and runtime identities. Parent runtime IDs are never inherited literally.
Genetic and germline prior dependencies are content-addressed and versioned. Fragile filesystem paths and silent fallback assets are prohibited.
Genetic complexity and inherited neural information are measurable so evolution and breed design can trade innate structure against lifetime learning.

The compact genome stores region floors and shares, connectivity-generator parameters, receptor profiles, plasticity parameters, developmental schedules, biochemical graph genes, mutation policy, and germline-prior manifests.

Development supports staged growth from newborn through mature life, including body growth, organ maturation, biochemical expression, neural growth, critical periods, puberty, senescence, and other species-specific stages.
Development receives authoritative biological age, genotype, current body and biochemical context, and previous developmental state; it outputs due expression and growth operations.
World time and biological age are distinct. A newborn created late in world history begins at biological age zero unless a specific reproductive mechanism says otherwise.
Biochemical signals may gate or modulate development, but biochemistry does not directly rewrite cognitive policy. It triggers genetically defined developmental responses.
Natural developmental brain growth and deliberate mature-brain augmentation use the same function-preserving graph-migration substrate with different policies.
Critical periods may alter plasticity, structural growth, receptor expression, teacher responsiveness, or region recruitment without making mature learning impossible by default.
Developmental operations that change graph topology occur at explicit transaction boundaries with checkpoint, provenance, and rollback support.
Developmental regions are generated by compact regional and connectivity programs rather than by storing every neuron and synapse in the genome.
A germline prior manifest names exact regional blocks, bridge blocks, schemas, compatibility families, source provenance, sanitization receipts, and inherited-information cost.
Germline prior blocks are immutable and content-addressed. A new breed revision creates new blocks or a new manifest; it never mutates an existing published block in place.
A germline prior is a sanitized newborn-compatible template, not a saved adult checkpoint with a memory table removed.
Prior blocks are region-addressable and may be recombined or selected independently when compatibility and bridge requirements are satisfied.
Bridge blocks or deterministic developmental bridge rules describe cross-region priors without requiring one monolithic whole-brain asset.

Personal episodes, named individuals, exact locations, private conversations, current body schema, current chemistry, current activation, pending eligibility, and unresolved action credit are excluded from germline priors.

Generic reusable representations and skills may be inherited after sanitization: object persistence, containment, affordance structure, generic navigation, manipulation priors, social prediction, and language-grounding priors.
Missing or incompatible germline assets cause explicit construction failure or an explicitly requested migration path. Silent substitution is prohibited.
Biochemistry owns chemical concentrations, reaction state, receptor/emitter state, endocrine regulation, metabolic intermediates, and biochemical developmental signals.

Biochemistry does not own final neural threshold, attention, salience, motor confidence, learning-rate, planning, or action policy values. It supplies signals; neural receptor phenotypes determine cognitive effects.
The biochemical phenotype contains a bounded sparse active set of chemical species with per-species baseline, decay, range, type, and compartment information.
The address space may support up to 256 species for compatibility and experimentation, while each phenotype instantiates a smaller active subset such as 32-64 species unless its budget permits more.
The biochemical phenotype supports sparse reactions with bounded reactants, products, stoichiometry, rates, compartments, and optional rate-control loci.
The biochemical phenotype supports emitters that map typed source loci to chemical release using bounded cadence, threshold, gain, analogue/digital response, inversion, and optional source reset.
The biochemical phenotype supports receptors that map chemical concentrations to typed body, organ, drive, developmental, autonomic, or neural loci.
The biochemical phenotype supports neuroemitters that map bounded neural summaries or learned assembly activity to chemical release.
Receptor and emitter destinations are typed and validated. Untyped raw pointers or arbitrary memory addresses are prohibited.
Different organisms may respond differently to the same chemical concentration because receptor expression, thresholds, gains, target loci, and neural receptor profiles are heritable and evolvable.

Material and energetic biochemical pathways obey declared conservation and resource accounting. Regulatory signalling chemicals may be produced and decay non-conservatively only through explicit emitters and costs.
Biochemical execution cost scales with active reactions, receptors, emitters, organs, and species, not the square of all possible chemical IDs.
Chemicals may act on different natural timescales, providing transient arousal, medium-duration reinforcement, slow developmental regulation, persistent toxins, and other temporal roles.

Compartmentalization may model blood, organ-local chemistry, extracellular signalling, gut contents, neural modulators, or other species-specific compartments without requiring every organism to instantiate every compartment.
A drive frame is a bounded derived view tied to authoritative body and biochemical state. It cannot advance independently.

Evolution can change what raises, lowers, suppresses, stores, or restores a drive by changing body, chemical, reaction, emitter, and receptor pathways while preserving the brain-facing ABI where required.
Emergency chemistry may suppress or transform lower-priority drive signals without hardcoding a complete cognitive decision tree.
A drive is not itself a reward. A high drive changes internal state and salience; the brain must still learn or infer which grounded actions affect it.
The neural receptor frame exposes bounded chemical/receptor activations with stable semantics, source chemistry version, target neural receptor class, and causal tick.
The neural-emission frame exposes bounded neural summaries to biochemistry without giving chemistry arbitrary access to raw neural state.

Neural receptor effects may modulate interoceptive input, regional excitability, projection gain, local threshold, attention gating, plasticity receptor classes, structural growth, sleep, and consolidation.
Those effects are computed by the neural phenotype from biochemical signals. Biochemistry does not publish one universal finished `NeuralModulation` policy object.
Neuroemitters allow learned cognition to influence autonomic, endocrine, developmental, social, and metabolic state without directly mutating body variables.
Reward valence, biological value change, and neural reward-prediction error remain separately represented and inspectable.
Every sealed experience transaction includes measured before/after body and biochemical references sufficient to compute actual homeostatic change.
A production outcome may not substitute a zero or default homeostatic delta when canonical biology changed.
Use a small multidimensional neuromodulatory vector rather than one universal scalar. Synapse or projection receptor profiles project that vector into a local third factor.
The organism can learn different things from the same physical event depending on its current physiology, expectations, receptor genetics, memory, and social context.
Adaptive neural compute is reserved for functions that materially benefit from learning, prediction, memory, context, generalization, arbitration, communication, or flexible control.

The brain supports sparse recurrent dynamics, nonlinear dendritic computation, local plasticity, predictive learning, attention, memory interfaces, semantic topology, factorized action selection, and structural plasticity.
No region name dispatches a handwritten cognitive algorithm. Region function emerges from connectivity, ports, dynamics, chemistry, plasticity, development, training, and experience.
The brain never receives game-specific commands such as `find food`, `attack target`, `solve task`, or an equivalent high-level policy shortcut as a sensory input or motor primitive.
The portable cognitive core has stable sensory, interoceptive, memory, semantic-prior, teacher/social, motor-intent, neural-emission, persistence, and inspection ports.
Neural state is recurrent and can preserve context, attractors, oscillations, working memory, and temporally extended competence.
Synaptic state has distinct inherited, lifetime-consolidated, and fast acquired components with explicit update, persistence, and inheritance semantics.
Lifetime and fast acquired weights are somatic. They do not enter offspring except through explicit sanitizing assimilation.
Neurons or projections may use different intrinsic time constants, update cadences, receptor profiles, plasticity classes, and metabolic costs.
Selected neurons support nonlinear within-neuron conjunction computation through bounded dendritic branches or an evidence-backed equivalent.
Dendritic execution is indexed by target or another sparse equivalent. It may not scan every branch for every neuron.
The neural substrate exposes enough bounded state for persistence, migration, debugging, work accounting, and capability attribution without placing identity indirection in the hot path.
High-volume recurrent projections, dendritic evaluation, local learning, and prediction heads are batch-executed on the GPU using sparse target-major or tile-major layouts.
Quantization, sparsity, batching, and accelerator-specific kernels may alter numerical precision only within declared behavioural and dynamical tolerances.
The nine founder homologues are permanent developmental and compatibility anchors. They cannot be deleted, although their mature functions and sizes may change above functional floors.
Founder region labels never authorize special handwritten cognitive code.
Region size, recurrence, cell mix, dendritic capacity, connectivity, receptor expression, plasticity, cadence, and developmental timing are phenotype-controlled and evolvable.
Founder allocation uses minimum floors plus proportional remainder so small brains preserve essential interfaces while larger brains devote most added capacity to flexible cognition.
Reference remainder shares are: Perceptual 16%, Interoceptive 6%, Association 23%, Temporal 13%, Executive 10%, Memory Interface 7%, Action/Planning 10%, Social/Communication 8%, Flexible Reserve 7%.
Evolution and development may create derived regions by reserve recruitment, subdivision, duplication and divergence, assembly specialization, bounded fusion, and pruning.
Every derived region records parent homology, creation mechanism, interface ports, prior dependencies, receptor/plasticity profile, capacity requirements, and compatibility family.
Derived-region count and capacity are bounded by brain class, developmental viability, inherited-information cost, and runtime work budgets.

Crossbreeding uses homology-aware bounded recombination. Matched derived regions recombine; unmatched regions are optional structural alleles expressed only when dependencies and budgets are satisfied.
New or unmatched bridges begin silent, zero-gain, low-gain, or in developmental acclimation. They may not immediately destabilize the child brain.
Sensory adapters expose grounded modality features, confidence, spatial/temporal reference, and provenance. They do not expose designer semantic categories as truth.
A body-neutral sensor ABI may normalize or compress raw signals, but must not secretly perform the semantic recognition, planning, or value judgement assigned to cognition.
Attention performs broad peripheral processing followed by bounded expensive focal processing or an equivalent mechanism that materially reallocates compute.
Focal selection depends on current physiology, memory, concepts, uncertainty, prediction residuals, social state, novelty, and learned neural influence.
Focal capacity is a function of brain class, phenotype, current state, and available compute rather than a universal fixed constant.
Changing attention while holding the world constant must be capable of changing downstream neural evidence or action, not only a diagnostic label.
Attention includes hysteresis and persistence so noisy small salience changes do not cause pathological target thrashing.
The peripheral pass is usually world/CPU efficient; focal sensory encoding and neural processing may be batched on the GPU. Exact placement is replaceable.
The cognitive context is bound to one organism, causal sequence, world tick, perception frame, and canonical body/biochemical view.
The context interoceptive view is populated from canonical biology. A default or stale internal-state vector may not coexist with a different authoritative state in the same decision.
Canonical digests are identity and integrity evidence. They are not semantic embeddings and may not be used as geometry for learning or generalization.
The context supports bounded explicit uncertainty, source confidence, recency, and provenance so cognition can distinguish observation, memory, semantic prior, and teacher communication.
The organism supports delayed episodic recall, context-sensitive retrieval, memory confidence, source/provenance, and forgetting or compression.
Memory retrieval provides evidence and expectancy; it does not force an action or bypass neural arbitration.
Candidate-specific episodic evidence may alter attention, prediction, neural state, or action preference through a real production path.
Individual semantic memory stores grounded concepts, relations, confidence, source, temporal validity, and contradiction history.
Personal semantic propositions and autobiographical episodes are not written into the germline by ordinary sleep or reproduction.
The Memory Interface region controls queries, retrieval, storage, and neural translation while the memory store remains an explicit bounded subsystem.
Memory can represent individuals and relationships persistently across time, save/load, sleep, separation, and reunion.
Memory consolidation balances retention, compression, interference control, and generalization without forcing all stable memories into neural weights.
Episodic memory is usually sparse irregular CPU-side storage with bounded GPU uploads for selected retrievals; alternative placements require measured benefit.
Concepts can form, strengthen, weaken, split, merge, decay, and be re-grounded from experience.
Concept induction is organized by predictive and cognitive utility, not only perceptual clustering.
Systematic contradiction may create or raise an unresolved gap and may trigger concept splitting, relation revision, targeted attention, or exploration.
Concept and gap state can alter neural context, attention, prediction, memory retrieval, communication, or action through explicit causal paths.
Global diagnostic maxima alone do not satisfy target-grounded concept or gap influence. Evidence must be linked to relevant objects, relations, actions, or contexts.

Concept induction and neural structural growth are separate learning processes. They may exchange bounded evidence, but concept edges are not automatically synapses and strong synapses are not automatically concepts.
External semantic-prior suggestions remain hypotheses until grounded. They cannot create authoritative concepts by declaration.
The brain predicts grounded successor features including sensory change, contact, motion, drive/chemical change, success/failure, concepts, social response, and other phenotype-supported targets.
Source and successor vectors use explicitly versioned semantically corresponding features or an explicit cross-schema mapping.
Prediction conditions on the full joint motor bundle, not only one primary action ID when multiple channels execute together.
Categorical motor identities use one-hot, learned, structured, or otherwise semantically valid encodings. Arbitrary integer or bit geometry is not treated as meaningful distance.
The predictive objective includes information-preserving constraints or grounded target construction that makes constant and action-insensitive representations non-optimal.
Different materially distinct successor states remain separable; different actions can predict different outcomes; passive observation can improve later prediction or behaviour.
Prediction is used before action to estimate candidate consequences, uncertainty, or information gain, not only updated after the fact.
Prediction residuals influence unresolved gaps, attention, curiosity, memory prioritization, learning, and structural proposals through bounded interfaces.

Stable targets may use EMA teachers, stop-gradient encoders, fixed projections, variance/covariance constraints, contrastive structure, grounded observables, or evidence-backed combinations. No one self-supervised family is locked.
The brain supports bounded counterfactual rollout or deliberation using its learned world model, initially at small depth and candidate count rather than exhaustive tree search.
The brain supports fast online learning that can alter behaviour after a small number of relevant experiences.
Eligibility is bound to the exact organism, phenotype/graph epoch, perception/context, selected joint motor output, and causal outcome transaction.
Every active motor channel can receive causally supportable credit through joint eligibility or channel-aware traces without fabricated channel reward labels.
Experience preserves individual channel commands and the joint physical outcome. It need not invent separable rewards for channels whose effects are inseparable.
Immediate plasticity and slower normalization/consolidation have distinguishable semantics, schedules, and evidence.
Negative physical/biochemical experience can produce an appropriate aversive learning signal and change later action preference through the ordinary production path.
Positive homeostatic improvement, novelty, social consequence, and prediction surprise can shape different receptor classes rather than collapsing into one universal reward.
Current hormone names may be reference species channels, but the architecture does not assume one universal mammalian mapping for every breed or transplanted brain.
Metaplasticity and local learning-rule parameters are heritable and can be optimized through founder meta-training and evolution.
A teacher, evaluation harness, or world script cannot directly set the neuromodulatory third factor as an answer key.
The lifetime brain supports experience-dependent synaptogenesis, pruning, dendritic branch allocation, and accepted structural changes that alter later computation.

Structural candidate discovery never enumerates all absent neuron pairs. Its complexity is approximately proportional to active structure times a bounded candidate budget, such as O(NK), O(BK), or better.

Candidate evidence may include coactivation, eligibility, prediction residuals, shared concept/gap support, local activity sketches, spatial/developmental affinity, and bounded stochastic exploration.
Candidate storage granularity is replaceable: neuron, branch, route, tile, sketch, or hybrid. No per-neuron reservoir is locked as universal architecture.
Dendritic conjunction capacity is allocated by phenotype, development, experience, and capability-per-compute evidence rather than uniformly or decoratively.
A structural counter, proposal object, or pruning-only path does not satisfy synaptogenesis. Accepted growth must change live sparse computation.
Structural changes are persisted, versioned by graph epoch, included in work accounting, and compatible with brain growth and rollback.
The brain can issue simultaneous bounded commands on multiple motor channels.
A motor intent bundle records every active channel, primitive/parameterization, intensity, duration, direction or target reference, confidence, coordination group, and causal sequence.

Inhibition is primarily within channels; learned coordination operates across channels. The architecture does not force locomotion, gaze, posture, manipulation, and vocalization into one exclusive token.
Orientation and sensor direction are real motor channels with production candidates, execution, outcome, learning, and persistence.
The motor ABI expresses body-neutral effectors and intentions, not game-specific semantic goals.
The brain can learn novel combinations of existing primitives and can adapt motor intentions to changed embodiment through the peripheral body-schema layer.
Parameterized motor primitives and learned synergies provide combinatorial behaviour without an explosion of discrete action IDs.
Deterministic actuator stabilization, inverse dynamics, servo loops, and safety constraints do not consume the portable cognitive neural budget.
The embodiment layer learns sensor calibration, effector controllability, proprioceptive body schema, motor synergies, and action-to-sensory consequences.
The embodiment adapter may not infer or choose semantic goals on behalf of the cognitive core.

A transplanted brain can discover a new embodiment through exploration, prediction, teacher guidance, and safe calibration rather than requiring hardcoded assumptions such as two legs or a forward camera.
Sensor and motor port descriptors are stable, typed, capability-oriented, versioned, and discoverable by the organism.
Embodiment-specific acquired state can be saved, replaced, retrained, or discarded independently of the portable cognitive core.
Organisms can enter, maintain, and exit sleep through biological state, external conditions, or explicit safety/recovery mechanisms.
Sleep may consolidate fast to lifetime weights, episodic and semantic memory, prediction, concepts/gaps, structural proposals, derived-region recruitment, and developmental neural growth.
All required sleep updates commit atomically for one cycle or roll back. Partial cross-system consolidation is prohibited.
Sleep does not directly mutate germline priors or offspring. Natural assimilation is a separate lineage process.
Sleep and replay are bounded by phenotype and work budgets and may prioritize salient, surprising, unresolved, socially important, or unstable experiences.
A completed sleep cycle can restore fatigue/energy state and can change later behaviour through actual consolidated cognition.
Replay identity, cycle identity, graph epoch, and persistence state prevent duplicate, stale, or out-of-order consolidation.
Semantic and memory systems reference persistent concepts, memories, assemblies, regions, and ports; they do not depend on raw synapse handles or GPU indices.
Every neuron has an individual-local lineage identity sufficient to track preservation, duplication, specialization, migration, and assimilation provenance.
Ordinary synapses, branches, and routes need not have permanent global IDs. They use deterministic graph-epoch handles and durable old-to-new migration manifests.
Structural recompaction, pruning, growth, expansion, and relocation can freely change physical indices while preserving logical identity and causal state.
Offspring inherit developmental homologues and priors, never the parent's runtime neuron or structural handles.
Both gradual developmental growth and deliberate mature augmentation use one function-preserving migration engine with mode-specific scheduling and safety policy.
Expansion occurs at a quiescent cognitive transaction boundary after pending action credit, weight-bank transactions, and replay state are committed or explicitly discarded.
Existing trained neurons, routes, memory anchors, concepts, predictor state, and learned dynamics remain the anchored core. Expansion does not randomly rebuild the old brain.

Allowed reference morphisms include silent neuron addition, neuron duplication with conserved contribution, common-mode-preserving recurrent blocks, zero-gain routes, dormant dendrites, residual identity paths, and self-distillation into new capacity.
Neuron duplication preserves aggregate downstream drive and recurrent common modes while newly introduced difference modes begin stable or contractive.
Additional capacity is recruited gradually through prediction of old regional state, residual-error learning, local self-distillation, and staged release of plasticity.
The enlarged brain must approximate the original brain's immediate behaviour and representative internal trajectories before new capacity is allowed to change policy substantially.
Every growth operation produces a pre-migration checkpoint, logical/physical map, graph-epoch manifest, added-neuron provenance, continuity receipt, and rollback path.
Somatic augmentation does not alter offspring until explicit genetic assimilation creates a new germline prior or developmental allele.
New capacity is preferentially allocated to Flexible Reserve, Association, Temporal-Predictive, Executive, Action/Planning, and Social/Communication unless profiling shows another bottleneck.
The founder species receives a viable pretrained neural and developmental foundation rather than random unusable cognition.
The published founder runs only through ordinary organism interfaces. No oracle feature, hidden label, direct action trace, or privileged trainer remains attached.

Founder pretraining covers generic competencies: object persistence, action consequence, body schema, navigation, avoidance, homeostatic learning, manipulation, social attention, imitation, and communication grounding.
Founder training varies worlds, object identities, curricula, embodiments, and sensor mappings enough to reduce benchmark or world memorization.
Training uses a nested outer loop that optimizes initial priors and how the creature learns during legal inner lifetimes.
Inner lifetimes inside meta-training use the same causal organism step, local plasticity, memory, chemistry, motor, sleep, and structural mechanisms available after deployment.

A trainer-removed acclimation phase demonstrates retained competence, continued learning, resistance to catastrophic forgetting, and absence of hidden teacher dependence before a founder prior is published.
Pretraining gives generic capabilities and priors, not game answers, fixed locations, private source-world facts, or a complete solved policy.
Semantic-prior requests contain bounded language or symbol context, a small set of active grounded concepts, model/interface version, and budget metadata.
Semantic-prior responses contain candidate relations, embeddings, distinctions, confidence, and provenance. They contain no creature action, reward, memory write, or policy command.

The semantic-prior service cannot inspect the full private episodic history, raw synapses, pending actions, or broad internal state unless a later architecture revision explicitly creates a safe interface.
A semantic hint is nonauthoritative. The creature must ground, accept, reject, revise, or ignore it through its own cognition and experience.
One shared service supports many organisms through caching, batching, event-triggering, and explicit token/latency budgets.
A mature creature retains substantial nonlinguistic intelligence and grounded competence when the semantic-prior service is disabled.
Breed genetics may evolve how much capacity and attention are allocated to semantic-prior integration without inheriting or duplicating the external model weights.
The teacher has a read-only pedagogical planner and an embodied teacher actor with separate authority.

The planner may inspect bounded curriculum progress, observable success/failure, developmental stage, available interfaces, coarse safety/homeostasis, uncertainty summaries, lesson history, and world state needed to construct lessons.
The planner cannot inspect raw synapses, neuron activations, eligibility traces, private episodic contents, hidden SLM state, pending action internals, or direct reward controls.
Only the embodied teacher actor influences the learner, through speech, gesture, demonstration, objects, environment arrangement, social response, and other ordinary world channels.
Teachers cannot directly write learner memories, concepts, weights, actions, rewards, neurochemistry, or declarations of understanding.
Teachers may be players, scripted agents, SLMs, larger LLMs, older creatures, or hybrids, provided they use the same grounded teaching interface.

Teaching episodes are auditable by curriculum ID, planner-visible diagnostics, teacher acts, learner-visible stimuli, learner response, physical/biochemical consequence, model provenance, and compute/token cost.
Learner competence is measured after the teacher is removed, not only while a capable external model is directing lessons.

A cultural package may contain language conventions, curriculum graphs, prerequisites, demonstrations, environmental setup recipes, social norms, tool-use procedures, assessments, and teacher capability requirements.
A cultural package does not directly alter genotype, germline neural priors, personal memory, neural weights, or biochemical state.
A breed may recommend or bundle a cultural package while remaining usable without it. Breed and culture dependencies are separately identifiable and removable.
Genetically similar populations can diverge culturally through teaching, imitation, language, environment, and historical contingency.

Research tooling can distinguish competence inherited genetically, acquired culturally, acquired individually without teaching, available only with the SLM, and available only while a teacher is active.
Reproduction uses canonical parent genotypes, physiological readiness, world interaction, and lifecycle authority to create a new child genotype and organism.
A child receives a newly developed brain with new neuron identities and no parent personal memory.
Compatible regional prior blocks and bridge blocks may be selected, blended, or recombined through explicit bounded recipes.
Ordinary births do not publish a new permanent large neural asset for every child. Child-specific compiled priors may be cached by content hash but remain derivable from genotype and dependencies.
Incompatible body, biochemical, neural, derived-region, or prior dependencies are detected before admission and either resolved through an explicit migration/crossing mechanism or rejected.
Parental investment, gestation/incubation, teaching opportunity, and social environment may influence development without becoming hardcoded inherited knowledge.
Natural assimilation can gradually alter developmental growth, receptor expression, connectivity affinities, plasticity, regional allocation, and small reusable motifs.
Natural assimilation is rare, lineage-level, information-budgeted, and does not publish a large new prior at every birth.
Breeder assimilation accepts a selected cohort and target competence, compares individuals, and extracts shared generalized organization.
One exceptional individual alone is not normally sufficient to define a new heritable prior without additional evidence, redistillation, or explicit expert override and provenance.
Assimilation uses cohort consensus, anonymization, compression bottlenecks, developmental redistillation, fresh-environment checks, and personal-memory leakage probes.
Assimilation excludes autobiographical episodes, individual identities, exact coordinates, private facts, current chemistry, current activation, pending eligibility, and body-specific calibration.
Assimilation may preserve generalized regional weights, motifs, assembly templates, connectivity affinities, receptor/plasticity profiles, and learning priors.
Every assimilated bit or parameter is charged against an inherited-information and developmental-complexity budget.
Published breed revisions are immutable, versioned, content-addressed, provenance-tracked, and independently testable from their source adults.

Evolution can alter morphology, metabolism, biochemical topology, developmental schedules, region allocation, derived regions, connectivity, receptors, plasticity, learning rules, temperament, and reproductive strategy.
Natural selection in game worlds is mediated by ecological survival and reproduction, not a hidden neural reward or externally assigned fitness during life.
Offline founder and research outer loops may use explicit fitness or loss functions, but their privileged optimization is training infrastructure and is removed at deployment.
Evolution should discover compact priors and effective learners rather than serializing complete adult solutions genetically.
A lineage objective may penalize inherited information, neural work, biochemical complexity, developmental fragility, and metabolic cost while rewarding survival and reproductive success.
Niches may favour cheap reflexive brains, larger flexible brains, specialized biochemistry, strong cultural learning, or other legitimate strategies.
Evaluation environments must monitor degenerate strategies such as inactivity, sensor exploits, reproduction loopholes, reward leakage, parasitic use of teachers, or trivial niche collapse.

A mature cognitive core can be exported with neural graph, acquired weights, concepts, unresolved gaps, episodic and semantic memory, predictor, attention state, learned personality-like tendencies, and language grounding.
Portable exports include exact dependency, graph-epoch, schema, germline-prior, semantic-prior ABI, and adapter compatibility manifests.

Full-organism transplantation may carry body and biochemistry; cognitive-core transplantation carries cognition plus an explicit receptor/viability interface but not the old transient chemistry by default.
A new game, software host, or robot supplies sensory, motor, and viability adapters. It may not replace the cognitive core with a host planner or arbitrary reward function.
A transplanted brain can reacquire body schema, controls, and local semantics faster than a newborn when its learned abstractions are genuinely general.
Transfer tests evaluate retention of object concepts, causal learning, social knowledge, language, planning habits, and learning speed across changed embodiment and environment.

Robot or software hosts may map battery, heat, damage, resource usage, and task constraints into a virtual physiology only through an explicit inspectable adapter. They may not inject hidden desirability labels.
Players can raise persistent individuals with visible needs, learning, relationships, language, habits, development, and personality-like differences.
Players can teach directly, construct schools and curricula, arrange environments, introduce cultures, and observe competence after teaching ends.
Players can select cohorts, breed lineages, cross compatible breeds, stabilize traits, perform breeder assimilation, and compare descendants.
Communities can exchange breeds, cultural packages, curricula, and exact individual exports as distinct artifact types.
Ecological communities can form persistent social structures, traditions, cooperation, conflict, resource practices, and cultural divergence.
Exceptional trained individuals may undergo deliberate brain augmentation or transplantation as a visible game/research process with risk, acclimation, and rollback.
The ordinary player interface emphasizes behavioural legibility and causal explanation. Raw synapse-level detail is reserved for expert inspection.
The game distinguishes inherited, learned, culturally taught, SLM-assisted, and currently teacher-dependent behaviour in inspection and lineage records.
Game convenience features must not silently bypass the organism's learning or causal systems when they are used as evidence of intelligence.
Breed, culture, and individual artifacts are semantically distinct and cannot be silently substituted for one another.
Community artifacts contain no executable native code. Data, declarative curricula, validated model references, and sandboxed scripts use explicit trust and permission policies.
Artifacts are content-addressed, schema-versioned, dependency-complete or exactly resolvable, provenance-tracked, and reproducibly loadable.
Licensing, authorship, source cohort, training cost, model dependencies, and compatibility are recorded for shared artifacts.
Missing dependencies and incompatible prior/adapter families fail explicitly rather than loading a superficially similar default.
All major subsystems expose deterministic hardware-independent work accounting sufficient for capability-per-compute comparison.

Conversion of cognitive or biochemical work to simulated metabolic cost is a configurable species/world policy, normally enabled in ecological/evolutionary worlds and optionally disabled in isolated benchmarks.
No neural, biochemical, attention, memory, teacher, or structural mechanism performs unbounded search or allocation.
The runtime supports benchmark tiers of 1, 10, 30, 100, and 500 organisms or equivalent progressive population scales, with results reported by brain/body class and active cadence.
Population scaling claims require measured wall time, GPU time, CPU time, memory, buffer traffic, work units, sleep bursts, teacher/SLM cost, and behavioural fidelity.
High-volume sparse recurrent and local-learning operations are GPU-batched; irregular sparse memory/topology/asset operations remain CPU-side until profiling supports relocation.
Inactive, sleeping, offscreen, or distant organisms may use reduced cadence or lower fidelity only through declared policies that preserve causal state and do not fabricate outcomes.
Logical IDs, provenance, and migration maps remain off the accelerator hot path unless measured evidence justifies a different design.
A mechanism must justify its compute cost through capability, robustness, evolvability, game value, or compression of other costs.

Exact saves contain world/ecology, body/organs, biochemistry, genotype and prior dependencies, developmental state, neural graph epoch, acquired weights/structure, memory, concepts, prediction, sleep, culture, adapters, and identity metadata.
Missing exact cognitive, biochemical, genetic, memory, or dependency state causes an explicit restore error or an explicit migration path, never silent default substitution.
Schema migrations are deterministic, versioned, auditable, and produce receipts identifying transformed or discarded state.
Save/load preserves later control behaviour and internal causal state within declared deterministic or numerical tolerance.
Brain growth, derived regions, germline blocks, culture, teacher provenance, and portable-core exports are represented in persistence schemas from the moment they become production mechanisms.
A checkpoint never stores unresolved references to temporary local paths or mutable remote assets.
Player-facing presentation exposes understandable needs, emotions, relationships, learning, development, sleep, culture, and lineage without requiring neural expertise.
Expert inspection can trace stimulus -> attention -> neural state -> motor intent -> physical outcome -> biochemical consequence -> learning -> changed later response.
Inspection distinguishes inherited prior, fast learning, lifetime consolidation, explicit memory, culture, SLM hints, teacher actions, and host/adapter effects.
Telemetry, presentation, reports, and debug snapshots are read-only derived views tied to authoritative versions and ticks.
Every external SLM/teacher call, assimilation operation, migration, structural change, save migration, and evaluation run has provenance and cost receipts.
Comments and reports may not describe a live required mechanism as diagnostic-only, optional, or deferred unless the architecture itself says so.
Invalid IDs, stale causal sequences, incompatible graph epochs, malformed assets, nonfinite state, and impossible ownership relations fail explicitly.
A failed multi-system action, sleep, reproduction, assimilation, migration, or restore transaction does not partially commit authoritative state.
Safe fallback states may protect the simulation from corruption or catastrophic body control, but they are observable and cannot masquerade as successful cognition.
Rollback checkpoints exist for brain augmentation, schema migration, breed publication, and other high-risk irreversible operations.
Repeated diagnostic expansion is not a substitute for source-level tracing and repair. Observability remains bounded and purpose-driven.
Long-running simulations can detect and isolate corrupted individuals or assets without silently contaminating lineages or shared priors.
Every compliance finding cites one or more stable architecture requirement IDs and exact source/evidence locations.
A test written specifically around a stub or fixture cannot certify a production capability unless the same semantic path is used in ordinary gameplay.
A passing causal test does not prove intelligence, usefulness, generalization, robustness, scale, or compute efficiency.
Behavioural capability claims include appropriate controls, fresh environments, and service-off conditions where SLM or teacher dependence is possible.
Mechanism attribution requires ablation or another credible causal comparison when multiple systems could explain the result.
Performance claims identify brain class, body class, population composition, update cadence, sleep state, hardware, precision, and configuration.
Compliance tooling can produce a requirement matrix without modifying this architecture document.
Few-shot avoidance: one or a few adverse grounded experiences reduce later selection of the relevant hazardous behaviour without a host rule.
Reversal learning: the creature updates when an earlier useful relation changes, without erasing unrelated knowledge.
Passive observational learning: watching another agent or event can improve later prediction or behaviour without direct action experience.
Delayed episodic recall: relevant past events influence behaviour after intervening time and context changes.
Concept generalization: learned structure transfers to novel instances while systematic contradiction can trigger refinement or splitting.
Targeted curiosity: unresolved gaps and prediction uncertainty cause information-seeking attention or action rather than indiscriminate novelty seeking.
Novel motor combination: the creature composes known factorized primitives in a useful new joint behaviour.
Continual-learning retention: new learning does not catastrophically erase earlier unrelated competence.
Experience-dependent structure: different life histories produce meaningfully different neural structure and behaviour.
Social learning and teaching: competence acquired through a teacher or peer remains after the teacher is removed.
Cultural transmission: a learned convention or skill can pass through teaching across generations without biological inheritance.
Genetic contribution: descendants inherit compact learning or skill priors without inheriting source adults' personal memories.
Crossbreed viability: compatible regional priors and derived-region alleles recombine without destroying founder interfaces or causing silent dependency loss.
Memory leakage resistance: germline priors fail probes for source identities, private facts, exact locations, and autobiographical episodes while retaining generalized skill.
Brain expansion continuity: a trained individual preserves immediate and dynamical competence across upward scaling, then makes productive use of new capacity.
Transplantation: a mature cognitive core reacquires a new embodiment or environment faster or more effectively than an equivalent newborn.
SLM independence: disabling the semantic prior reduces only the capabilities legitimately dependent on it and does not erase grounded core intelligence.
Teacher independence: disabling the teacher after training preserves acquired competence and does not reveal hidden teacher-side policy execution.
Evolutionary usefulness: heritable variation in body, chemistry, development, cognition, or learning produces measurable, nontrivial selection gradients across generations.
Capability per compute: added neural, biochemical, memory, SLM, or teacher cost is justified by measurable capability, robustness, adaptability, or game value.
Use layered fast checks for contracts and causal boundaries, focused GPU checks for accelerator semantics, milestone end-to-end journeys, and separate statistical capability/scaling campaigns.
Full corpora, 500-organism profiles, long soaks, or evolution runs are not repeated against unchanged commits/configurations when exact valid receipts already exist.
Expensive validation waits until known source-level defects in the measured path are repaired, unless the purpose is explicitly to measure the defective baseline.
Code is graded against the target architecture even when migration is incomplete. Unimplemented target mechanisms remain gaps, not optional reinterpretations.
Migration supports compatibility layers that reproduce current founder species behaviour while new genetics, biochemistry, neural receptors, priors, and adapters are introduced.
Compatibility layers are versioned and temporary. They may not become hidden permanent authorities that bypass the new subsystem boundaries.
The current fixed drive/hormone controller may serve as a reference breed phenotype during biochemical migration, but it is not the permanent biochemical architecture.
Current Rust types, Bevy entities, WGSL layouts, N512/N2048 assumptions, IDs, constants, and test fixtures do not define permanent architecture.
Each migration phase produces a requirement-based compliance report, state/schema map, preserved capability list, unresolved gaps, and rollback plan.
Earlier architecture documents are archived with a notice that they are non-normative. Their requirement IDs, if any, may be mapped to new IDs for history but do not retain authority.
Bounded counterfactual planning with learned rollouts at greater depth and breadth.
Open-ended region duplication and specialization beyond initial bounded derived-region policies.
Large-scale robot deployment with real sensors, actuators, safety certification, and long-duration autonomous operation.
Cross-world software-agent embodiment with tools, files, and external services represented through grounded adapters and virtual physiology.
Evolved compact local plasticity programs or tiny meta-learned update networks, provided they remain bounded, inspectable, and accelerator-friendly.
Indirect developmental encodings such as CPPN-like generators, coordinate networks, or learned graph grammars for efficient neural and biochemical topology generation.
Neural and biochemical region duplication as an explicit evolutionary innovation mechanism with homology discovery.
Differentiable or surrogate models of organism development and lifetime learning for more efficient founder meta-training.
Shared community teacher ecosystems in which trained creatures teach younger creatures without an external LLM.
